xref.title: Reason for North American Cover Change (2001)
xref.body: The decision to use the scientific bubble chamber image for the North American cover of "Is This It" was made by The Strokes themselves, as they found it "a lot cooler" than the international nude shot. However, by the time singer Julian Casablancas contacted the label, the first edition of the album had already been pressed with the international cover. Consequently, buyers in North America during July and August 2001 received the original cover before the bubble chamber shot became standard. "When the band stumbled on the bubble chamber picture, they just thought it was a lot cooler and they wanted it to be the cover of the album for the world."

xref.title: Band Formation and Early Members
xref.body: Julian Casablancas and Nikolai Fraiture met at age six while attending a prestigious French school in New York City. Julian met Albert Hammond Jr. at the Institute Le Rose, a highly expensive private boarding school in Switzerland. By 1997, Julian and Nick Valensi were at Dwight School, where they met Fabrizio Moretti and started a band. Albert moved from Switzerland to New York for film school, became Julian's roommate, and joined the band, with Nikolai joining shortly after as the bassist. "By 1997, Julian and Nick were attending a college prep school called the Dwight School. Again, not cheap."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Name Origin
xref.body: The band played their first gig under the name The Strokes on September 14, 1999, at The Spiral in New York. The name "The Strokes" has no special story; Julian Casablancas blurted it out during rehearsal, and the group adopted it because it was the name everyone hated the least. "There's no special story behind the name, The Strokes. It's just one that everybody hated the least."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Struggles and Financial Support
xref.body: In the late 90s, the New York rock scene was considered dead, with few venues beyond private parties in Brooklyn warehouses. The Strokes worked through these challenges with Albert Hammond Jr.'s father's credit card and part-time jobs. Julian Casablancas was a bartender at Max's Kansas City, Nikolai Fraiture worked at a video store, Fabrizio Moretti made smoothies, and Albert Hammond Jr. worked at Kim's video. "Along with Albert's dad's credit card, they also had part-time jobs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence on Julian Casablancas
xref.body: Julian Casablancas, The Strokes' lead singer and chief songwriter, learned to write songs by figuring out Nirvana riffs. This foundational influence helped shape his approach to songwriting. "He learned to write songs by figuring out Nirvana Riffs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Influence on Julian Casablancas
xref.body: Julian Casablancas' mother, a former Miss Denmark, was instrumental in introducing him to bands like The Doors, shifting his musical focus away from Phil Collins records. "Mom was a former Miss Denmark who pried Julian away from his Phil Collins records and got him into bands like The Doors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Is This It Album Title and Covers
xref.body: The band's debut album was titled "Is This It," intentionally without a question mark because it was felt that "it looked wrong." The album featured two different covers. The original cover depicted the photographer's naked girlfriend, fresh out of the shower, with a black glove as a prop, creating a "spinal tapish" effect. Julian Casablancas later suggested a second cover, an image of subatomic particles from a physics experiment at CERN in Switzerland, which was adopted due to label concerns about displaying the naked woman in stores, particularly in the "puritanical US." Releases in July and August 2001 featured the original cover, while all subsequent releases used the second. "No question mark because it was felt that it looked wrong."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Julian Casablancas Solo Projects
xref.body: Julian Casablancas has released solo records under his own name. Additionally, he formed and released two albums with a band called The Voids. "Julian has won under his own name and two with a band he called The Voids."

xref.title: Julian Casablancas' Background
xref.body: Julian is the son of John Casablancas, founder of the Elite Model Management Agency, which managed stars like Cindy Crawford, Stephanie Seymour, Gisele Bündchen, Linda Evangelista, Naomi Campbell, Kendall Jenner, Pauline Apport's Gova, Claudia Schiffer, and Heidi Klum. His mother, a former Miss Denmark, encouraged his interest in bands like The Doors, moving him away from Phil Collins records. Julian had a teenage drinking problem, leading him to rehab in high school, which he attributed to his environment, rebelling to be closer to his father. The connection to the modeling agency proved useful, as models from Elite would attend early Strokes gigs, helping with attendance. "He's the son of John Casablanca's, the founder of the famous Elite Model Management Agency."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Julian Casablancas' Folding Electric Bicycle Patent
xref.body: In the fall of 2015, Julian Casablancas filed for a patent for a folding electric bicycle that did not have pedals. The patent listed Richard Priest, The Strokes' tour manager, and Warren Foo, their video director, as co-inventors alongside Casablancas. "In the fall of 2015, Julian filed for a patent for a folding electric bicycle. No pedals."

xref.title: Trust Fund Band – Most Members from Wealthy Families, Casablancas Money Bankrolled Early Career
xref.body: Almost every member of The Strokes came from wealthy backgrounds. Singer Julian Casablancas is the son of John Casablancas, head of the Elite Model Agency, home to Cindy Crawford, Linda Evangelista, Claudia Schiffer, Tyra Banks, Cameron Diaz, and Heidi Klum. Julian attended a private school in Switzerland where he met Albert Hammond Jr., the son of 1970s singer-songwriter Albert Hammond ("It Never Rains in Southern California"). Drummer Fabrizio Moretti's parents sent him to the Dwight School, a Manhattan prep school, where he met Julian and guitarist Nick Valensi — the only relatively modest-background member. Bassist Nikolai Fraiture grew up in a two-bedroom apartment with five relatives but still attended a prestigious bilingual school on the Upper West Side. The Casablancas family money funded the band's early gear and operations. "No wonder so many other bands were jealous."
